title: ESSAY 2: The Rise of Non-Performing Assets in Indian Banks — Causes, Consequences and Cures

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: A loan is classified as a Non-Performing Asset (NPA) when interest or principal installment remains overdue for more than 90 days in standard loans or two crop seasons for short-duration agricultural crops.
Primary causes of rising NPAs include aggressive lending practices, unviable project appraisals, governance failures, policy paralysis, and macroeconomic downturns.
High NPAs give rise to the 'Twin Balance Sheet' problem, constraining bank lending capacity, depressing corporate investment, and slowing overall economic growth.

Major legal and institutional cures include the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code (IBC) 2016, Asset Reconstruction Companies (ARCs), National Asset Reconstruction Company Limited (NARCL), and the SARFAESI Act 2002.

blocks.content: Non-Performing Assets reflect not just financial stress on bank balance sheets, but a deeper structural constraint on credit growth and overall macroeconomic stability.

rows: Total value of all loans defaulted by borrowers in the bank's portfolio
The actual bad asset value remaining after deducting provisions set aside by the bank
Gross NPA = Total Non-Performing Loans / Total Advances
Net NPA = Gross NPA - Provision Coverage Amount
Measures the overall quality of loan origination and risk management
Reflects the actual financial risk and balance sheet burden faced by the bank

items: Distinguish between Gross NPA and Net NPA: Net NPA = Gross NPA minus Provisioning.
Understand the Special Mention Account (SMA) classification: SMA-0 (1-30 days overdue), SMA-1 (31-60 days overdue), and SMA-2 (61-90 days overdue).
Focus on key judicial and regulatory mechanisms like the IBC 2016, DRTs (Debt Recovery Tribunals), SARFAESI Act, and RBI's Prompt Corrective Action (PCA) framework.
